deep.reconstruction:
The page states one identity and a table of values. Throughout, F(s) := sum_{n>=1} n^{1-s}/(e^{2 pi n}-1), for s in C.

(1) Ramanujan writes F(s) = S_s - (1/2) zeta(s-1) + (3/(4 pi)) zeta(s) + (pi/12) zeta(s-2). On this page S_s is not defined. The line works as a definition of S_s (equivalently, a normalisation of the remainder); its general analytic definition must be in the text being compared, presumably Hardy's paper (see the pencil note). What the page actually supplies is the values of S_s for s = 0 (mod 4).

How the values arise (my reconstruction). Write b_k = B_k/k!.
- Case s = 4m+4 (exponent 1-s = -(2N+1) with N = 2m+1 odd). Put alpha = beta = pi in the Lerch/Ramanujan transformation for zeta(2N+1). This gives F(s) + (1/2) zeta(2N+1) = -2^{2N-1} pi^{2N+1} sum_{j=0}^{N+1} (-1)^j b_{2j} b_{2N+2-2j}.
- The two end terms (j = 0 and j = N+1) total zeta(s)/(2 pi).
- The terms j = 1 and j = N total pi zeta(s-2)/6. For N = 1 these coincide in a single term worth pi zeta(2)/12.
- So S_s is the remaining rational multiple of pi^{s-1}, after Ramanujan's chosen multiples 3/(4 pi) and pi/12 of zeta(s) and zeta(s-2) are taken out.
- Case s = -4n, n >= 1. Here F(-4n) = sum n^{4n+1}/(e^{2 pi n}-1) = B_{4n+2}/(8n+4) (Glaisher/Ramanujan). This equals -(1/2) zeta(-4n-1). The zeta(-4n) and zeta(-4n-2) terms vanish (trivial zeros), so S_{-4n} = 0.
- Case s = 0. sum n/(e^{2 pi n}-1) = 1/24 - 1/(8 pi). The right side is S_0 + 1/24 - 3/(8 pi), so S_0 = 1/(4 pi).
- Case s = 4. sum 1/(n^3(e^{2 pi n}-1)) = 7 pi^3/360 - zeta(3)/2. The right side is S_4 - zeta(3)/2 + pi^3/120 + pi^3/72, giving S_4 = 7 pi^3/360 - 8 pi^3/360 = -pi^3/360.
- Case s = 8. sum n^{-7}/(e^{2 pi n}-1) = 19 pi^7/113400 - zeta(7)/2. The two zeta terms give pi^7/12600 + pi^7/11340 = 19 pi^7/113400, so S_8 = 0.
- Case s = 12. sum = 1453 pi^11/851350500 - zeta(11)/2. Subtracting 3 zeta(12)/(4 pi) + pi zeta(10)/12 leaves (4359 - 2073 - 2275) pi^11/2554051500 = pi^11/232186500.
- Case s = 16. By the Bernoulli-product formula the bracket is about -5.685e-15, so S_16 is about 8192 x 5.685e-15 pi^15 = 4.657e-11 pi^15. This agrees with pi^15/21470872500.
- Cases s = 20 and s = 24. S_20 = 191 pi^19/398240480137500 and S_24 = 907 pi^23/184177171143590625 are stated. They follow from the same finite Bernoulli sums; I have not checked them by hand.

(2) The pencil note in another hand reads 'Compare G.H.H., A formula of R. (Journal)'. This refers to Hardy, 'A formula of Ramanujan', J. London Math. Soc. 3 (1928).

(3) Context. The previous page is on theta-function identities. The next page is on Voronoi-type Bessel series for divisor-like sums.
errors: No mathematical errors detected in the values I checked (S_{-4n}, S_0, S_4, S_8, S_12, S_16). S_20 and S_24 were not hand-checked.

S_s is never defined on the page. The identity is meaningful only alongside a definition supplied elsewhere (presumably Hardy's paper). Read alone, it is a normalisation that is verified only at s = 0 (mod 4).
S_{-4n} = 0 must be read for n >= 1, since S_0 = 1/(4 pi) is nonzero.
In S_4 the denominator 360 appears to be written over an earlier figure (possibly 180). The final 360 is correct.

results.what: Decomposition sum n^{1-s}/(e^{2 pi n}-1) = S_s - zeta(s-1)/2 + 3 zeta(s)/(4 pi) + pi zeta(s-2)/12, with S_s vanishing at s = -4n (n >= 1) and s = 8
results.modern_name: Ramanujan's formula for zeta(2n+1) / Lerch's formula at alpha = beta = pi; Mellin-transform residue decomposition of a Lambert series
results.usually_credited_to: Lerch (1901) and Ramanujan (Notebooks, Entry 21 of Ch. 14) for the zeta(4m+3) case; this general-s form was published by Hardy (1928, 'A formula of Ramanujan')

results.modern_name: Evaluations of sum n^{-(4m+3)}/(e^{2 pi n}-1) in terms of zeta(4m+3) and Bernoulli numbers
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan / Lerch; tabulated in Berndt's editions

results.modern_name: Glaisher-type Lambert series evaluation (Eisenstein series at i)

deep.surprise_reason: The values are consequences of Ramanujan's well-known zeta(2n+1) formula. The general-s form was published by Hardy in 1928 under the title 'A formula of Ramanujan', as the pencil note itself points out. The page is a correct, explicit table but contains nothing not already attributed to Ramanujan.

checkable.asserts: Exact Bernoulli-number form of S_16/pi^15 equals 1/21470872500 (difference 0)

transcription_corrections: S_16 denominator is 21470872500 (single number). The transcription's '2147087250 0' is a split artifact.
Pencil note reads 'Compare G.H.H. A formula of R. (Journal)', i.e. Hardy, 'A formula of Ramanujan', J. London Math. Soc. 1928.
In S_4 = -pi^3/360 the denominator appears overwritten (possibly over 180); the final reading 360 is correct.
The zeta symbols are written as a long-s-like glyph; zeta(s-2) in the last term (transcribed correctly).
